title: Full linearisation and invariant diagonal give an equivalence between smooth degree-k graded bundles and symmetric k-fold vector bundles with the core identity condition
author: Andrew James Bruce; Janusz Grabowski; Mikołaj Rotkiewicz
difficulty_reason: The inverse construction averages weighted coordinate systems over the symmetric group and proves that the resulting triangular coordinates identify the invariant diagonal as a graded bundle. It must also recover all equivariant multiple-vector-bundle morphisms from their restrictions to that diagonal, using symmetry of the polynomial coefficients. This global equivalence requires more than ordinary polarization of a single homogeneous polynomial.

proof_review.note: Complete2.24 proof and full-linearisation/iterated-tangent support2.1-2.6 read. The source constructs the canonical symmetric-group maps, defines their group-composition and transposition-core identities, averages homogeneous coordinates, proves a triangular invertible coordinate change and the exact permutation action, obtains the invariant fixed submanifold and total weight, and proves fullness/faithfulness from the symmetric coefficient transformation law. Prior graded-bundle homogeneity and ordinary linearisation/jet embedding are established background. Coordinate factorial conventions and the worked2.25 diagonalisation example are bundled. No degree-two symplectical, N-manifold or superisation variant counted.

statement_scope: k>=1, ordinary smooth real graded bundles of degree k with the author homogeneous polynomial transition laws. The target consists of k-fold vector bundles equipped with isomorphisms sigma_g:D->D^g for every g in S_k satisfying2.19 and sigma_(i,j)=identity on each double-vector-bundle core C_ij as in2.20; morphisms intertwine all sigma_g. L=l^(k-1) and F(D)=S_k-fixed diagonal with the total weight field are quasi-inverse functors. Arbitrary balanced bundles without the symmetry/core conditions and supermanifolds are excluded.
